Govt to finalise Liberation War martyrs list: Minister
2026-04-29T15:34:49+06:00 | Star Online Report
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/govt-finalise-liberation-war-martyrs-list-minister-4163791

Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan has said that even after so many years of independence, a complete list of martyrs and victims of genocide from the Liberation War has not yet been prepared.

He assured that the government has taken the initiative to compile such a list. Through this initiative, an accurate and accepted record of all martyrs and genocide victims will be created, ensuring proper recognition and honour for their sacrifice.

The minister made the remarks during the parliamentary question-and-answer session chaired by Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad today, in response to a question from Pirojpur-3 MP Ruhul Amin Dulal.

Replying to the question, the minister said the number of gazetted Liberation War martyrs under the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs is 6,480.

According to the data, this includes 3,698 gazetted civilian martyrs, 1,541 gazetted armed forces martyrs, 817 gazetted BGB martyrs, 423 gazetted police martyrs, and one gazetted Ansar force martyr.

In response to a question from Cumilla-9 MP Abul Kalam, Azam Khan said that based on recommendations from the Liberation War Council, 6,476 names have been removed from gazettes, Lal Muktibarta, or Indian lists since 2010. Of these, 481 cancellations took place from last August to date.

Meanwhile, Agriculture Minister Mohammed Amin Ur Rashid, replying to a question from Sirajganj-4 MP Rafiqul Islam, said that 11,005 fertiliser dealers are currently engaged across the country to ensure uninterrupted supply to farmers.

Responding to a question from Gopalganj-3 MP S M Jilani, the agriculture minister said that of the existing dealers, 5,669 were appointed by BCIC and 5,336 by BADC. The government has compiled a list of 2,311 dealers accused of irregularities and policy violations.

Verification of their information is ongoing, and depending on the severity of the irregularities, dealership cancellations and punitive measures will be taken, followed by the appointment of new dealers.

In response to a question from Jamalpur-2 MP AE Sultan Mahmud Babu, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister Afroza Khanam said a tourism master plan is being prepared, targeting 5.57 crore tourists and the creation of 2.194 crore employment opportunities by 2040.
